name: Samlah
overview: Samlah was a male Edomite who served as king of Edom, succeeding Hadad in the royal line. He was from the city of Masrekah, as recorded in the genealogies of Genesis. His role as king places him within the historical context of Edomite leadership following the descendants of Esau.
namesAndTitles: The name Samlah appears as a proper name in Scripture without a given meaning or divine origin. It is simply recorded as the name of this Edomite king in Genesis 36:36.
familyAndRelationships: Samlah is identified as a descendant of Esau, linking him to the Edomite lineage. Beyond this, Scripture does not provide additional family relationships for him apart from his kingship and tribal affiliation.
scriptureSignificance: Samlah's significance lies in his position as a successor to Hadad as king of Edom, highlighting the continuation of Edomite governance after Esau's descendants established their territory. His mention in Genesis underscores the biblical record of the Edomite kings who ruled before Israel had kings, illustrating the historical and genealogical framework important to understanding the nations surrounding Israel.
